about: Independent test data for 3D-printed polycarbonate and PC-CF, set beside the makers' datasheets in materials.json, for the mount's design values (printed-mount [3JA], [Xtj]). Collected 4 Oct 2026. XY: specimen printed flat, load along the layers; Z: specimen printed upright, load across the layers. Every figure is copied from the source as published; 'verified' says how it was read: 'full text' (read in the paper or page itself), 'abstract only' (the paper is paywalled; only its abstract was read), 'second-hand' (quoted by a third party, the primary document not read). null: not reported. No figure here is estimated; estimates and assumptions live in allowables.json, labelled.

sources.who: Stefan Hermann, CNC Kitchen (independent tester; filament supplied free by Prusa for review)
sources.title: Prusament PC Blend Review
sources.material: Prusament PC Blend (PC compounded with undisclosed polymers, no styrene). Not one of our three candidates; the nearest published independent test of a consumer PC filament with flat and upright specimens.

method.settings: PrusaSlicer built-in profile: 275 C nozzle, 115 C bed, 20% part fan
method.specimen: his own mini tensile specimens (not an ISO/ASTM geometry), printed flat (XY) and standing (Z); DIY universal test machine at constant speed; bending modulus from his 3-point rig with dead weights
method.infill_walls: not stated on the public page (full report on Patreon)
method.dried: both: spool stored open in a damp basement for a year (un-dried), then 6 h in a food dehydrator at its highest setting

sources.notes: Upright 'dried brass' 43.4 MPa is derived from his statements (layer strength +73% over the steel-nozzle 25 MPa, and 23% above the un-dried 35 MPa). The key finding for us: a hardened steel nozzle cut layer strength by about 40% against brass, probably thermally. The X1 Carbon ships with a hardened steel nozzle.

sources.who: Gomez-Gras G., Abad M.D., Perez M.A., IQS School of Engineering, Universitat Ramon Llull (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Mechanical Performance of 3D-Printed Biocompatible Polycarbonate for Biomechanical Applications

method.printer: Stratasys Fortus 400mc, heated build chamber; 365 C extrusion; T16 tip, 0.254 mm layers
method.standards: tensile ASTM D638 type IV, 4 mm thick; 3-point bending ASTM D790; shear ASTM D5379; Charpy ISO 179-1; flexural fatigue ASTM D7774 procedure A (3-point) on a Bose ElectroForce 3200
method.orientations: X-Flat, X-Edge (layers parallel to load) and Z-Flat (upright, load across layers); raster 0, +/-45, 90 deg
method.annealed: not stated for the specimens (supplier post-processing oven 145 C is mentioned as a supplier condition)
method.n: 5 per static configuration; 3 per fatigue load level

sources.notes: Industrial printer with a heated chamber, so its layer bonding is better than an open or passively warmed desktop machine's. Even so, at 20% of static bending strength every configuration failed within 4,000 to 40,000 cycles: printed PC is poor in fatigue.

sources.who: Rodrigues A., Branco R., Franco M., Silva R., Malca C., Martins R.F., NOVA University Lisbon, University of Coimbra, Polytechnic of Leiria (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Mechanical, Fatigue, and Thermal Characterization of ASA, Nylon 12, PC, and PC-ABS Manufactured by Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF)

method.printer: Stratasys Fortus 450 (heated chamber); PC 275 C extrusion, 110 C platform; 0.254 mm layers
method.standards: ASTM D638-03 specimens, about 5.2 mm thick; quasi-static at 2 mm/min; fatigue at 10 Hz, R = 0.05 (tension-tension), load controlled sine, staircase method, run-out 1e6 cycles
method.infill_walls: 100% infill; micro-CT still shows voids, concentrated mid-section

sources.notes: PC had the lowest fatigue strength of the four materials. The paper's stated fatigue limit (3.6 MPa, Table 11) and its Table 6 (3.74 MPa maximum stress at 7%) differ slightly; the percentages are computed on a strength of about 53.4 MPa, not the 57.1 MPa of Table 4. Recorded as published. Extrapolating the Basquin fit to 1e7 cycles gives about 1.9 MPa (3.3% of 57.1 MPa): that is our extrapolation, labelled in allowables.json.

sources.who: Fang L., Yan Y., Agarwal O., Yao S., Seppala J.E., Kang S.H., Johns Hopkins University and NIST (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Effects of Environmental Temperature and Humidity on the Geometry and Strength of Polycarbonate Specimens Prepared by Fused Filament Fabrication
sources.verified: full text (figures not digitised; percentages from the text)

method.printer: LulzBot TAZ 6, 0.5 mm nozzle, 0.3 mm layers, 10 mm/s, in an acrylic enclosure with a heater (room to 90 C) and dry-air purge (<10% RH)
method.specimens: tensile, longitudinal (along the bead) and transverse (across the bond)
method.dried: filament dried 1 h in vacuum at 100 C, then conditioned at 10 to 90% RH for the humidity series

results.chamber_temperature_effect_longitudinal: slight increase with chamber temperature, not significant (p = 0.024 per the paper's own reading); approaches bulk PC when printed at 90 C
results.transverse: brittle; strongly anisotropic; chamber temperature effect not significant (p = 0.273)

sources.notes: Dry filament printed close to bulk PC along the bead; wet filament lost about 30% of it through porosity. Supports a moisture knock-down and the rule that PC is dried and fed from a dry box.

sources.who: Akgumus D., Istanbul Aydin University (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Experimental and Statistical Evaluation of Infill Density Effects on the Mechanical Properties of FDM-Printed PLA, ABS, PC, and PETG Engineering Materials

method.printer: GEMA AFZ 227, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, 60 mm/s, 280 C nozzle, 120 C bed, grid infill, raft; 25 C, 40% RH room
method.infill_walls: 30% and 60% grid infill; wall count not stated

results.modulus: reported as 14.6 to 15.9 GPa for PC, not physically plausible for PC (bulk about 2.4 GPa); not used

sources.notes: Strength on the nominal section. Against a solid printed PC of about 59 MPa (independent typical, allowables.json) that is about 0.30 at 30% and 0.42 at 60% infill. Supports designing load paths solid.

sources.who: Aldawood F.K., Abualkhair H.F., Khan M.A., Alquraish M., University of Bisha and others (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Optimization of Mechanical Properties Using Fused Deposition Manufacturing Technique: A Systematic Investigation of Polycarbonate and Polylactic Acid Specimens

method.orientations: horizontal and 'vertical' (from the dimensions, on edge, layers still along the load, not upright Z)
method.n: 1 per condition (the authors say this is underpowered)

sources.notes: One specimen per condition: low weight. Shows the spread of flat XY PC strength (42.5 to 55 MPa) from one lab.

sources.who: Remache A., Pavon W., Jara Vinueza O., Chicaiza J., Fuentes J.M., Cadena H., Universidad Central del Ecuador and others (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Sterilization-Induced Property Changes in FDM-Printed Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Polycarbonate for Medical Device Applications
sources.material: Prusa Polymers PC-CF (Prusament PC Blend Carbon Fiber). The only independent printed PC-CF tensile result found.

method.printer: Smart3D Macro (enclosed), 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, 275 C nozzle, 110 C bed, 55 mm/s

sources.notes: The reported modulus (175 MPa) and elongation (65%) are not plausible for PC-CF (bulk PC alone is about 2400 MPa and the datasheets give 2 to 3% elongation); probably from crosshead travel without an extensometer. Only the strength is used. No Z data.

sources.who: Dogan O., Kahramanmaras Sutcu Imam University (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Short-term Creep Behaviour of Different Polymers Used in Additive Manufacturing under Different Thermal and Loading Conditions
sources.journal: Strojniski vestnik - Journal of Mechanical Engineering 68(7-8):451-460, 2022
sources.verified: full text (creep curves in figures only, not digitised)

method.printer: Ultimaker 2+ Extended, 270 C nozzle, 110 C bed, 45 mm/s, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, lines infill
method.specimens: printed then CNC-milled to the creep geometry, ASTM D638/D2990

results.summary: PC crept least of the six materials (PLA, tough PLA, ABS, CPE, PC, nylon) in every case; no PC specimen ruptured, including 60 C at 20 MPa; no rupture of any material at 25 or 40 C

sources.notes: Only three hours. Says PC is the best of the common filaments in creep, and that 40 C is not a cliff for it; does not give a long-term strain we can design to.

sources.who: Salazar Gabino A.G., Perez M.A., Garcia-Granada A.A., Reyes G., Puigoriol-Forcada J.M., IQS, Universitat Ramon Llull (peer reviewed)
sources.title: A study of creep in polycarbonate fused deposition modelling parts

results.summary: creep of FDM PC depends on build orientation, raster air gap and number of contours, in line with their static findings; primary and secondary creep fitted with Bailey-Norton and a fractional model

sources.notes: Numbers not read. Worth buying if creep turns out to govern.

sources.who: Puigoriol-Forcada J.M., Alsina A., Salazar Gabino A.G., Gomez-Gras G., Perez M.A., IQS, Universitat Ramon Llull (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Flexural fatigue properties of polycarbonate fused-deposition modelling specimens

results.summary: S-N curves at R = -1 and R = -0.5; build orientation significantly affects fatigue; FEA with Goodman correction on the R = -1 curve predicted a real part well

sources.notes: The method (von Mises plus Goodman on the printed S-N curve) is the one to follow for the walking case.

sources.who: Sedighi I., Ayatollahi M.R., Bahrami B., Perez-Martinez M.A., Garcia-Granada A.A., Iran University of Science and Technology and IQS (peer reviewed)
sources.title: Mechanical behavior of an additively manufactured poly-carbonate specimen: tensile, flexural and mode I fracture properties
sources.notes: Agrees with Gomez-Gras: printed PC modulus is nearly isotropic, strength is not.

sources.who: Covestro, Makrolon 2805 injection-moulding datasheet (a resin maker, independent of the three filament makers; moulded, not printed)
sources.notes: Bulk PC creep: the modulus falls about 21% in 1000 h at room temperature (ISO 899-1 uses small strain, about 0.5%). Printed PC has interfaces and voids and is expected to creep at least as much; we extrapolate to years in allowables.json, labelled.

sources.who: Mu Q., Ningxia University and Xi'an Jiaotong University (peer reviewed data paper)
sources.title: Experimental data for creep and dynamic mechanical properties of polycarbonate and polycarbonate/ABS
sources.verified: full text (curves in the Mendeley dataset, not read)
sources.material: neat PC, machined dog bones (not printed)

results.note: loads chosen below 0.8 of yield; ruptured at 47 to 52 MPa, the 41 MPa test stopped by hand because rupture took too long

sources.notes: Even bulk PC ruptures in creep at about 0.7 to 0.8 of its yield strength: a sustained-load factor well below 1 is needed.

sources.who: Bambu Lab (manufacturer; comparison point only, not independent)
sources.title: Bambu PAHT-CF Technical Data Sheet V3.0
sources.verified: second-hand (quoted by a review site; the PDF itself was not reachable)
sources.notes: A maker's own Z penalty for a short-fibre composite: half the XY strength across the layers. Used only to bound the PC-CF Z assumption.

not_found.bambu_pc: No independent test of Bambu PC (along or across the layers) was found, 4 Oct 2026. Its own datasheet's Z/XY tensile ratio (56/62 = 0.90, annealed and dried 80 C 12 h) is far above every independent result (0.35 to 0.61).
not_found.polymaker_polymax_pc: No independent test of PolyMax PC with published numbers was found. CNC Kitchen compared PC Blend against it (2021) but the PolyMax numbers are not on the public page; a search summary claimed a Z/XY of 63%, which could not be traced to a source and is not used.
not_found.3dxtech_carbonx_ezpc_cf: No independent test found. Its datasheet gives no Z values. The only independent printed PC-CF figure is Remache 2026 (Prusa PC-CF, XY strength only).
not_found.polymaker_fiberon_pc_cf: Polymaker's Fiberon line lists PA6, PA612, PA12, PET and PPS CF grades; no Fiberon PC-CF was found.
not_found.printed_pc_long_term_creep_strain: No published long-term (months to years) creep strain for printed PC at room temperature was found open-access; Salazar 2018 has creep curves but is paywalled.
not_found.printed_pc_cf_creep_fatigue: No creep or fatigue data for printed PC-CF was found.
